newsitem.title: INDIA: Blue-chips finish lower at India's NSE.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips finish lower at India's NSE.

text.p: Share prices ended the year on a dull note at India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Tuesday, with blue-chips closing with small losses, dealers said.
Trading was largely limited to squaring up of positions by speculators in front-bencher stocks, they said.
"Basically, speculators were unwinding long positions," said chief dealer Sanjeev Choithani at brokers Pashupati Advani.
Other stock markets including the Bombay Stock Exchange were closed on Tuesday. They reopen on Wednesday after seasonal holidays.
The benchmark 50-stock index of the NSE lost 14.15 points, or 1.58 percent at a provisional close of 897.55, off its intra day high of 922.05.
The boards of Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Ltd (ICICI) and SCICI on Tuesday approved a proposal to merge the two institutions, an ICICI statement said.
It said the merger would be effective April 1, 1996.
The swap ratio would be two shares of ICICI for every five of SCICI, the statement said. ICICI shares rose 1.15 rupees to 62.0 in volumes of 245,450 shares.
SCICI fell 1.65 rupees to 25.50, off 29.25 with 91,000 shares traded.
ITC lost 1.40 rupees to 330.55, SBI 1.15 to 234.45, Reliance 2.65 to 206.0, ACC 29.10 to 1,226.0, TELCO 8.0 to 340.0, BSES 5.75 to 212.75 and MTNL 9.50 to 230.0.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said he expected to present the 1997/98 (April-March) budget on time at the end of February, the Press Trust of India said.
The minister made his remark to reporters after launching the Finance Ministry's home page on the Internet on Tuesday.
